question: Alpha-blockers are an appropriate first-line treatment for a 28-year-old man presenting with a slow, splaying urinary stream and a progressive reduction in flow rate over 12 months.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct — false. Alpha-blockers target the prostate and will not relieve a urethral stricture. A young man with obstructive lower urinary tract symptoms should be investigated for stricture with retrograde urethrography before any medical therapy is started.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: This is actually false. In a young man, the likely diagnosis is urethral stricture, not BPH. Alpha-blockers are prostate-directed and ineffective for stricture; urethrography (RGU/MCU) and urethroscopy are the investigations needed.
